chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to him, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hamid al-Attar narrated to him, who said: Al-'Ala' ibn Razin narrated, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

Regarding the words of God, the Exalted: '...there was beneath it a treasure for them.' He said: By God, it was not gold or silver, but only a tablet containing four phrases: 'Indeed I am God, there is no god but Me, and Muhammad is My Messenger. I wonder how one who is certain of death can have a happy heart; I wonder how one who is certain of reckoning can laugh; I wonder how one who is certain of destiny can find God slow in providing his sustenance; I wonder how one who sees the first creation can deny the second creation.'
ai.seo_question: What was the spiritual treasure buried beneath the Prophet's grave according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) interprets the 'treasure' of the two orphans not as gold or silver, but as a spiritual tablet inscribed with four profound theological reflections on certainty (*yaqin*). These insights—regarding death, reckoning, divine decree, and resurrection—serve as practical keys to maintaining inner peace and gratitude, reflecting the Shia emphasis on contemplative faith over material accumulation.
